title: Model Flavor Catalog: Mapping Model Variants to Customer Personas and SLA Sensitivities
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a definitive catalog of 'model flavors' (size/quantization/latency tiers, embeddings vs completion-optimized, rerank-ready variants) and map each flavor to target customer personas and typical SLA/cost sensitivities. The goal is a pragmatic product-facing artifact used by sales, solutions, and provisioning tooling to recommend default model variants and fallback strategies for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog includes at least 12 distinct model flavors and machine-readable tags for quantization, throughput tier, max-seq support, and intended workload (chat, embed, rerank, summarization)
Each flavor is mapped to 3 customer persona archetypes (SMB SaaS, AI-native startup, regulated enterprise) with notes on typical SLA/cost trade-offs
Recommendations for default flavor per persona and a fallback chain for capacity or cost-triggered degradations
A short-playbook for sales/SEs with recommended pricing levers and sample benchmarking numbers (latency p50/p95 and $/k tokens)
work_items: Inventory current catalog from model-team and runtime performance bench (ENG to supply CSV)
Define persona archetypes with GTM and CS (PM to run 3 interviews)
Run micro-benchmarks across 5 representative latency/cost configs (bench script, 1 day)
Author machine-readable flavor schema and sample JSON lines for the catalog
Publish doc to Confluence and create a view in Console's model-picker (UX stub)
decisions: Use three primary persona buckets for mapping: SMB SaaS, AI-native (growth), Regulated Enterprise
Adopt a simple flavor tagging schema: {workload, quant_level, throughput_tier, latency_profile, cost_bucket}
Default recommendation engine will prefer lower-cost quantized flavors for non-latency-sensitive SMB routes
Fallback chain will prioritize compatible architectures to avoid tokenization/compatibility regressions
